description:
## Problem
After the corpus rule change no official TPC-DS run can be stamped official, and the nightly release canary (tests/integration/test_tpcds_official_submission.py) fails. Official must follow the specification's definition of a valid run. Reproduced on the corpus rule head 8218cfa86b with tests/integration/test_tpcds_official_submission.py (record the command and log path); the first red nightly run id is added when the corpus rule merges.

## Change
- New phase qualify, after generate and before load, always in official mode and opt-in elsewhere (--phases qualify,...). It loads a separate SF 1 database (fixed suffix; DataFrame: a separately loaded context) on the same platform, driver, tuning and translation, so the power test still follows the load (TPC-DS 7.4.4.1; TPC-H 5.1.1.2, 5.3.1.4).
- The writer stamps official only when all hold: official mode; derived class full_spec; no failed query and no FAILED row evidence of any kind; validation.qualification.status passed; summary.validation passed or no_reference (benchbox/core/results/schema.py _recorded_compliance_class).
- The corpus rule adds a receipt whose status is not passed to validation failure (refused on both paths), and the shared roll-up (crr-v1) treats validation.qualification.status other than passed as failed. A missing receipt changes nothing (stored files have none).
- Every official run executes its own qualification; a receipt from another run is never reused, even with identical identity (owner decision 3).
- Clearing official on a timeout stays (mark_timed_out in benchbox/utils/run_deadline.py).
- The bundle validator's 'official only with a passing receipt' check is a format check; crr-a6, which lands after this item, lists it on its allowlist (recorded in crr-a6). Name the check in this pull request's body.
- Risk to record in the pull request: some cloud platforms may need extra privileges for a second database.
- Strengthen the release canary: official class, summary.validation passed, a passing 103-statement receipt, at least one PASSED measurement row in power and in throughput, no undocumented skip, no FAILED evidence. Add a TPC-H SF 1 official twin.

## Decision gates
- The stamp change and the phase land together in one pull request; if either cannot land, neither does.
- A failed qualification or a failed integrity check refuses the run (owner decision 2).
- While the release canary is red (from the corpus rule merge until this item lands), no release is cut (owner decision 8). If a release is about to be cut in that window, stop and report.

## Verification rubric
- Canary: tests/integration/test_tpcds_official_submission.py, TPC-DS and TPC-H, DuckDB SF 1, through make heavy-run (log path recorded).
- Writer: one parametrised test per official condition; flipping any one condition clears the stamp.
- Receipts: a failed, missing, out-of-run or copied receipt is each refused by both validators.
- Phases: a non-official run without --phases qualify records the same phase list as before and creates no '<name>_qualification' database.

## Guardrails (apply to every step of this plan)
- Fix the root cause for every platform and benchmark. No rule, check, exception, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix; only the pvm items may name Polars, and only to run and stage that run's files.
- Never edit a stored result file. Stored outcomes change only through the rule; any change shows in the committed snapshot diff (scripts/corpus_compliance_snapshot.py) and is explained per bundle in the pull request body.
- No new stored class value. No reader decides anything from benchmark.compliance_class, conformance_class or summary.tpc_metrics.suppressed.
- One implementation per concept: reuse existing helpers; make duplicate-check-delta stays at +0; no second copy of the rule, the roll-up, the row decision or the qualification comparator.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). User-facing changes add a changelog.d fragment; never edit CHANGELOG.md.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run, after make heavy-status, with command, maximum run time and log path announced first. No live cloud runs. Never touch the lock, set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force or BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off.
- Work in a linked worktree on the step's feature batch. Each batch is one pull request; run the local review before opening it; fix hosted-review findings. If the hosted review cannot complete, split the pull request so a reviewer can read it (owner, 2026-11-24). Never post a stand-in or adjudication, except on published-results pull requests, which follow the owner decision of 2026-11-24: an independent review with no Critical or Required findings, then a stand-in that cites it.
- Paths and line numbers were read on 2026-11-25 at the corpus rule head; re-read before editing and report drift instead of guessing.
- At a decision gate, follow the recorded owner decision. If its stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner; never substitute a different decision.
- Owner decisions: crr-00-corpus-rule-remediation-plan context, entries of 2026-11-22, 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25. Design: the spec-faithful validation plan summarized in crr-00 (qualification test, integrity checks, official-mode sequence).
